milestone.title: Raul Watch tab — launch, attach, lifecycle graph, queue, logs, and agent progress

intent.outcome: A human can open Raul's dedicated Watch tab, select one or more watch-drivable milestones, run mp's authoritative preflight, explicitly start the watch flow, and follow the active milestone across its full lifecycle and current mp watch stage while retaining safe stop, detach, attach, resume, log, and agent-output controls.

problem.description: Raul currently has no interface for mp watch. Its existing W/w behavior is only a 30-second Overview auto-refresh toggle and does not start agents, select milestones, display watch stages, attach to a run, or expose watch logs and pane output. Humans must leave Raul, invoke mp watch manually, inspect herdr or files separately, and mentally map lifecycle changes to the automation stage. The desired workflow is a dedicated tab where selection, preflight, start, progress, control, and final outcome are visible in one place.

in_scope: Add a dedicated `Watch` lane immediately before `Settings` in Raul's tab order
Remove the existing Overview W/w auto-refresh mode, its local timer/countdown state, footer wording, keybind surface, and tests so the term Watch refers only to the mp watch workflow
A milestone picker containing all mp-watch-drivable lifecycle states: approved, in-progress, self-reviewed, reviewed, and remediation, while excluding non-drivable milestones
Support one milestone or an ordered multi-milestone queue; queue order is the order in which the user selects milestones
Run `mp watch --dry-run <ids...>` as the sole preflight after selection, present every returned dependency/configuration/eligibility diagnostic, and keep Start disabled until the dry-run passes
A distinct explicit Start action after successful preflight; starting invokes the mp watch control surface from M178 rather than reproducing watch logic inside Raul

A simple ASCII lifecycle graph covering the full canonical milestone lifecycle, highlighting the selected milestone's current lifecycle and identifying the active mp watch stage and role within that lifecycle, including the remediation loop
For queues, one detailed graph for the active milestone plus a compact ordered queue showing pending, active, completed, skipped, failed, exhausted, stopped, or otherwise mp-reported outcomes
Refresh lifecycle, active stage, queue state, structured watch-log tail, and active-role agent output every two to five seconds without blocking keyboard input or rendering
Show `.mp/watch.log` tail plus output from the herdr pane belonging to the currently active runner/coordinator stage; automatically switch pane output as the active role changes
When opening the Watch tab, detect an existing run and prompt before attaching; monitor a live process without launching another driver, and offer Resume for stale/interrupted state
Run controls for graceful Stop, Detach, and Resume/attach; switching tabs leaves the run active
When quitting Raul during a live run, present Stop and exit, Detach and exit, and Cancel choices
Keep the latest completed, failed, skipped, exhausted, or stopped run's final graph and concise result visible across Raul restarts until another run replaces it
Mirror mp watch's existing queue continuation, skip, failure, stall, interruption, and exit-outcome semantics rather than implementing a Raul-specific policy
out_of_scope: Editing agent/watch configuration inside the Watch tab or redirecting into an inline setup form
Automatically installing herdr, installing harness integrations, or repairing missing configuration
Selecting draft, groomed, complete, cancelled, deferred, blocked, or otherwise non-watch-drivable milestones
Parallel execution, manual drag/reorder controls, mp-path-derived ordering, or changing queue order after Start
A separate lifecycle graph for every queued milestone; only the active milestone gets the detailed graph
Side-by-side runner and coordinator panes or a manual role selector; output follows the active stage's role
A selectable history of multiple previous runs; only the latest terminal run persists
Changing mp watch lifecycle, remediation, prompt, pane-reuse, or sequencing behavior owned by M178 and existing mp watch milestones
Web UI, desktop notifications, remote control, or highly artistic graph rendering

design_decisions.choice: Watch is a dedicated lane immediately before Settings
design_decisions.rationale: The user wants Watch to be a navigable workflow, not an Overview viewing mode, while keeping Settings last.
Keeping both meanings would preserve the naming confusion that prompted this feature. Manual Overview refresh remains distinct.

design_decisions.choice: Select queue, run mp watch --dry-run, review diagnostics, then explicitly Start
design_decisions.rationale: The user requires a dependency/configuration check before execution and chose an explicit start rather than auto-start on valid selection.
The Watch tab reports missing herdr/configuration data but does not install dependencies or edit settings.

design_decisions.choice: All watch-drivable states; single or ordered multi-selection in selection order
design_decisions.rationale: The UI must support fresh and continuable milestones, both single and queue runs, without inventing mp-path or manual reorder policy.

design_decisions.choice: Full canonical lifecycle plus active mp watch stage and role
design_decisions.rationale: Lifecycle alone is too coarse and watch stages alone lose milestone context; the combined view answers both where the milestone is and what automation is happening.

design_decisions.choice: One active detailed graph plus a compact ordered queue
design_decisions.rationale: This preserves detailed progress without multiplying large ASCII graphs for every queued milestone.

design_decisions.choice: Poll and redraw every two to five seconds
design_decisions.rationale: The user prefers timely progress without the subprocess and rendering churn of sub-second updates.

design_decisions.choice: Prompt to monitor a live run; resume only stale/interrupted state
design_decisions.rationale: This avoids duplicate watch drivers while preserving recovery.

design_decisions.choice: Tab changes keep running; Raul exit offers Stop, Detach, or Cancel
design_decisions.rationale: The automation must not stop because the user inspects another lane, but quitting requires an explicit ownership decision.

design_decisions.choice: Structured watch log plus automatically selected active-role pane output
design_decisions.rationale: The watch log explains orchestration while the active agent output explains the work occurring at the highlighted stage.

design_decisions.choice: Persist and restore the latest terminal run only
design_decisions.rationale: The user wants the final graph to survive Raul restarts without expanding scope into run-history management.
Raul is the human control and observation surface; mp remains authoritative for sequencing and outcomes.

work_packages.name: Watch lane migration
work_packages.goal: Remove the legacy Overview watch meaning and introduce a dedicated Watch lane before Settings on the post-M172 tab model.
work_packages.rollback: Restore the old Overview refresh toggle and remove Lane::Watch as one coordinated revert.

work_packages.name: Selection and start
work_packages.goal: Model watch-drivable milestones, ordered selection, authoritative dry-run preflight, and explicit start through M178.
work_packages.rollback: Leave the Watch lane read-only with Start disabled while preserving all other Raul lanes.

work_packages.name: Graph and live observability
work_packages.goal: Render lifecycle/stage progress, queue outcomes, watch log, and active-role pane output on a bounded cadence.
work_packages.rollback: Fall back to status-only Watch rendering and manual refresh without changing the running mp process.

work_packages.name: Attach and process controls
work_packages.goal: Support live monitoring, stale resume, stop, detach, quit choices, and latest terminal-result restoration.
work_packages.rollback: Disable control actions and keep the tab as a read-only monitor of M178 state.

work_packages.name: Raul regression verification
work_packages.goal: Prove responsive rendering, input smoothness, tab navigation, and exact mp outcome passthrough across the full Raul suite.
work_packages.rollback: Revert the failing UI slice while retaining the stable M178 control plane.

steps.action: Remove the Overview W/w auto-refresh feature end to end: App timer/deadline fields, ToggleWatch action, keybind/config setting, mode dispatch, countdown footer, runner idle tick, and dedicated tests, while preserving manual Overview refresh.
steps.done_when: No Raul source/config/help/footer path exposes toggle_watch or watch countdown state, W/w no longer changes Overview, and r/R still reloads Overview.

steps.action: Add Lane::Watch immediately before Settings, update labels, tab order, digit jumps, narrow overflow layout, mouse hit areas, and post-M172 lane-count tests.
steps.done_when: Wide and narrow tab bars render Watch directly before Settings, keyboard/mouse navigation selects it, and all positional lane tests use the new count/order.

steps.action: Add a lane-scoped Watch client model and M178 adapter, load only approved/in-progress/self-reviewed/reviewed/remediation milestones, support single or ordered multi-selection, and preserve selection order as the queue.
steps.done_when: Entering Watch produces a drivable-only picker, selection order is stable, and no other lifecycle can enter the start queue.

steps.action: Run mp watch --dry-run with the selected ids, render all structured precondition and milestone diagnostics, and expose a separate explicit Start action only after a successful preflight.
steps.done_when: Empty/failed preflight cannot call start or herdr; successful preflight keeps its queue visible and requires a second explicit Start command.

steps.action: Start the validated single milestone or queue through M178's detach-safe control command, pass ids in selection order, disable duplicate Start, and keep the run active across normal tab switches.
steps.done_when: One explicit Start launches one driver with the exact queue, repeated Start is blocked, and leaving Watch invokes no stop/detach command.

steps.action: Implement a testable ASCII graph for the full canonical lifecycle with current lifecycle, active mp watch stage and role highlighting, an explicit reviewed-remediation-self-review loop, and a compact ordered queue beside/below the active graph.
steps.done_when: Every lifecycle node renders at supported widths, remediation is visibly a loop rather than success, and only the active milestone receives the detailed graph while all queue outcomes remain visible.

steps.action: Add a non-blocking two-to-five-second Watch poller that reads M178 status/result, tails bounded .mp/watch.log entries, requests active-role output, and mutates App only when observable data changes.
steps.done_when: Synthetic clock tests prove polling stays within the selected cadence, keyboard input remains responsive, subprocess failures are non-fatal, and no redraw storm occurs.

steps.action: Render the newest structured watch-log rows and bounded output from the role active at the current stage, switching automatically between runner and coordinator and showing unavailable output as a diagnostic.
steps.done_when: Stage-role changes select the corresponding pane output on the next poll, log/output regions remain bounded, and missing panes never close the TUI.

steps.action: On Watch entry, classify M178 state and prompt before monitoring a live run; offer explicit Resume only for stale/interrupted state and restore terminal state without launching a driver.
steps.done_when: Live Attach is read-only, stale Resume launches one resumed driver, terminal state opens as a result, and canceling the prompt performs no mp mutation.

steps.action: Wire graceful Stop, Detach, and Resume/attach actions plus a quit-during-live-run modal offering Stop and exit, Detach and exit, or Cancel; respect configured quit/escape bindings and never stop on tab navigation.
steps.done_when: Each modal choice invokes exactly its M178 command or no command, Stop is graceful, Detach leaves the driver live, Cancel remains in Raul, and tab switching is side-effect-free.

steps.action: Restore M178's latest terminal run on Raul restart and keep the final graph, queue outcomes, and concise complete/failed/skipped/exhausted/stopped result until a new run replaces it, without reinterpreting mp outcomes.
steps.done_when: A fresh App reconstructs the latest terminal display from mp, a new start clears/replaces it, and displayed queue/failure semantics match M178 fields exactly.

steps.action: Extend the existing tab, state, mode, render, and smoothness targets with Watch scenarios and run the full Raul regression suite after the lane-count and event-loop changes.
steps.done_when: All ten AC behaviors are covered in existing resolvable targets, narrow/wide rendering is stable, and every pre-existing Raul test passes.

findings.description: AC-07 VIOLATION — Watch log pane never displays content. crates/raul/src/tui/render/watch.rs:154-157 hardcodes `let plan_dir = std::path::Path::new(".");` (commented 'placeholder') and `let log_lines: Vec<String> = Vec::new();` — the renderer NEVER calls `tail_watch_log`. The pane always renders '(no log lines yet)' regardless of .mp/watch.log content. The function `tail_watch_log` (crates/raul/src/tui/watch.rs:1025) exists and has passing unit tests (tui_state.rs:542, 550), but no production path invokes it — L1 (green tests ≠ correct behavior). AC-07 explicitly requires 'The lower Watch view shows recent structured entries from .mp/watch.log'. Wire the canonical plan_dir through and call tail_watch_log(plan_dir, 8); add an integration test that drives the renderer against a fixture with log content.

L13 anti-pattern (dead-code shim to silence clippy). crates/raul/src/tui/render/watch.rs:188-193 carries `#[allow(dead_code)] fn _lane_dummy(_: Lane) {}` whose only purpose is to keep the `use crate::tui::app::{App, Lane};` import (line 28) referenced so the dead-imports lint stays quiet. The comment at line 188-191 admits as much. This is exactly the L13 lesson pattern documented in docs/code-review-lessons.md. The fix is to delete both the function and the unused `Lane` from the import (rg confirms Lane is referenced only inside _lane_dummy in this file).

AUDIT-TRAIL FRAUD (L5 + L18 violation). M179 AC evidence stamps claim 'External review F-01..F-08 (4 blockers, 2 majors, 1 lesson, 1 nit) all remediated' (per AC-01..AC-11 evidence text + commit 2c2edd9 message). But `mp reviews finding list 179 --summary` returns {fixed:0, open:0, total:0} and `mp reviews list` has NO M179 entry. The milestone was promoted to lifecycle=complete without any Stage-8 external review actually filed. The 'F-01..F-08' in the commit message refer to in-session self-review notes that were never persisted to the plan. Per the two-round review discipline (docs/code-review-lessons.md L5; mp-coordinator reviewing.md), self-review is round-1 only; the coordinator's Stage-8 review is mandatory and recorded. Also: the severity vocabulary in the evidence ('blocker', 'major', 'nit') is the stale four-level legacy set — SeverityRank::from_config_value (crates/mp/src/config.rs) treats those as None, defeating AC-06 of M147. Remediation: this external review (F-02..) IS the first real Stage-8 review; after closure, run mp reviews pass 179 --verdict ok --reviewer external-agent (opencode).

parse_preflight ignores documented JSON fields (L26 — docstring/impl drift). crates/raul/src/tui/watch.rs:561-652 — the docstring at lines 567-577 documents the mp watch --dry-run JSON shape including `blocked: false`, `next_action`, `stage`, `target_lifecycle`, `herdr_commands`, `prompt_preview`, `override_diagnostics`. The implementation only consults `ready` and `error`. If M178 ever emits `ready: true, blocked: true` (informational block alongside a passing gate), the candidate is classified DepStatus::Ready and Start is permitted. The picker test sample_payload (line 1157) even includes `M10 ... 'blocked': true` with a comment claiming 'the dry-run (S4) surfaces the blocked verdict as DepStatus::Blocked' — but parse_preflight never reads `blocked`. Fix: either narrow the docstring to drop the unused fields, or consult `blocked` (parser-side) before trusting `ready`.

has_live_run ignores stale-but-alive PIDs. crates/raul/src/tui/watch.rs:790-796 returns true ONLY when `status.kind == "live" && status.pid_alive`. A 'stale' classification with an alive PID (zombie, herdr orphaned, system clock skew) would return false, allowing start_watch to proceed and spawn a duplicate driver. The comment at lines 700-707 explicitly says 'M178's double-spawn guard does not catch the detach path' — this raul-side guard is exactly where that gap is closed, but it only covers the live case. Fix: also reject when kind == 'stale' && pid_alive, or surface a Resume prompt (classify_recorded_state already distinguishes Stale).

stop_watch gives no user feedback on no-op stop. crates/raul/src/tui/watch.rs:1079-1108 returns Ok(report) regardless of report.stopped. apply_action (action.rs Action::WatchStop arm) discards the report. When the user invokes Stop on a non-live run (e.g., race: run finished between status fetch and keypress), mp returns stopped=false with a human message ('no live run; nothing to stop') that is parsed into report.message but never surfaced to app.watch.last_error or any flash. AC-08 implies the user gets feedback on Stop. Fix: when !report.stopped, set app.watch.last_error = Some(report.message) or surface via app.flash_message.

AC-06 VIOLATION — Watch view does not refresh without a keypress. crates/raul/src/tui/runner.rs:421-452 — run_loop sets `needs_render = false` after the render phase (line 434) and only re-sets it to true inside dispatch (lines 504, 523). The on_idle closure at line 447 calls `poll_watch_state` which mutates `app.watch.status` / `app.watch.output`, but the post-on_idle path NEVER sets `needs_render = true`. Then `source.wait_next()` at line 498 blocks indefinitely. Net effect: poller updates state but the screen redraws only on the next keypress. AC-06 requires 'Graph, queue, active stage, log tail, and active-pane output update on a 2-to-5-second cadence without requiring a keypress'. Fix: set needs_render = true after on_idle when poller reports a state change (e.g., return a dirty bool from poll_watch_state, or compare app.version() before/after).

render_lifecycle_graph brackets every node, not just the active one. crates/raul/src/tui/watch.rs:824-846 — the per-node format string is `format!("{marker}{label}<")` where `<` is appended UNCONDITIONALLY to every node. `marker` is '>' for active and ' ' otherwise, but the closing `<` is always there. Output reads `>draft<-groomed<-approved<-in-prog<-self-rev<-reviewed<-complete<-cancelled<-remediation< ↺` — every inactive node carries noise, and the active node's closing `<` is visually indistinguishable from the rest. AC-05 requires 'readable ASCII graph, highlights the active milestone's current lifecycle'. Fix: only append `<` when *node == active. No test pins the inactive-node shape (tui_state.rs render_lifecycle_graph_no_active_lifecycle_uses_spaces checks the no-active path but the with-active path is untested for the bracketing).

tail_watch_log reads entire file into memory. crates/raul/src/tui/watch.rs:1025-1040 — `std::fs::read_to_string(&path)` then `body.lines().rev().take(n).rev()`. For a multi-MB .mp/watch.log (a long-running watch session produces substantial JSONL), this is a full-file read + full-line Vec allocation on every poll tick. Not wired into the poller today (see F-02), but the API contract invites a perf cliff the moment it is. Fix: bounded reverse read (seek from end, read last N KiB, split, take), or memoize the tail with an inode/mtime check.

on_idle error handler is silently broken. crates/raul/src/tui/runner.rs:447-452 catches on_idle errors with: if let Some(msg) = e.downcast_ref::<String>(). But poll_watch_state returns Result<u64, anyhow::Error> — anyhow errors wrap their underlying source type, they are NOT bare Strings. anyhow::Error::downcast_ref::<String>() returns Some ONLY when the error was constructed by Err(String.into()) (rare). Normal ?-propagated errors (io, serde, mp_runner failures) will downcast to their inner type, not String. The handler silently drops every real failure. The accompanying comment (Failures from the closure surface as last_error on app.watch and never bubble out of the run loop) is false today. Fix: use app.last_action_error = Some(format!({e:#})) unconditionally on Err, or match on a structured error type.
